extDescription.message: Spintax templates for manual outreach: fill contact forms and chats from your list, one row at a time. Local, no accounts.

stepFollowup.description: Follows "Step 2" and an em dash; the delay input and stepFollowupDays finish the line: "Step 2 — follow-up, [3] days after the previous step".

stepFollowupDays.description: Follows the delay input; see stepFollowup for the whole line.

stepDelayAria.description: Accessible name of the delay input.

demoBannerSent.message: Demo: nothing was sent. Mark the row as sent in the side panel to move on.
demoBannerSent.description: Banner on the bundled demo pages after a harmless "submit".

cmdActionTitle.description: Tooltip of the toolbar button and title of the Firefox sidebar.

cmdFill.message: Fill the mapped fields on the current page
cmdFill.description: Keyboard shortcut description in the browser's shortcuts UI; truncated past ~60 characters.

cmdCopyOpen.message: Copy the message and open the target
cmdCopyOpen.description: Keyboard shortcut description in the browser's shortcuts UI; truncated past ~60 characters.

cmdMarkSentNext.message: Mark as sent and go to the next row
cmdMarkSentNext.description: Keyboard shortcut description in the browser's shortcuts UI; truncated past ~60 characters.

cmdNextRow.description: Keyboard shortcut description in the browser's shortcuts UI; truncated past ~60 characters.

wizStepImport.description: Step chip 1 of the campaign wizard. One word — the five chips share one row.

wizStepRoles.description: Step chip 2 of the campaign wizard: give each column a role and settle duplicate rows.

wizStepProfile.description: Step chip 3 of the campaign wizard: who writes and what is written.

wizStepProblems.description: Step chip 4 of the campaign wizard: rows that cannot be sent as they are.

wizStepQueue.description: Step chip 5 of the campaign wizard: go through the rows by hand in the side panel.

wizImportHint.message: CSV / TSV / XLSX, or paste from Sheets. Roles are detected from values.
wizImportHint.description: Status line under the step 1 heading before a file is chosen. The file formats are file extensions — keep them.

wizFileLabel.description: Label of the file picker on wizard step 1.

wizOrPasteLabel.description: Label of the paste box on wizard step 1, the alternative to picking a file.

wizPastePlaceholder.message: Paste rows copied from Google Sheets / Excel (tab-separated)…
wizPastePlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the paste box on wizard step 1.

wizSheetLabel.description: Label and accessible name of the dropdown that picks a sheet of a multi-sheet XLSX file.

wizSheetOptionOne.description: Sheet dropdown item: the sheet name as written in the file, and how many rows it holds.

wizSheetOptionFew.description: Sheet dropdown item: the sheet name as written in the file, and how many rows it holds.

wizSheetOptionMany.description: Sheet dropdown item: the sheet name as written in the file, and how many rows it holds.

wizSheetOptionOther.description: Sheet dropdown item: the sheet name as written in the file, and how many rows it holds.

wizPastedTable.description: Stands in for the file name in the import status line when the rows came from the paste box.

wizFileError.description: Import failed: the browser's own error message follows and stays untranslated.

wizNoRowsFound.message: No rows found — check the first line holds headers.
wizNoRowsFound.description: The chosen file or pasted text parsed to nothing usable.

wizRowsOne.description: Row count in the import status line.

wizRowsFew.description: Row count in the import status line.

wizRowsMany.description: Row count in the import status line.

wizRowsOther.description: Row count in the import status line.

wizColumnsOne.description: Column count in the import status line.

wizColumnsFew.description: Column count in the import status line.

wizColumnsMany.description: Column count in the import status line.

wizColumnsOther.description: Column count in the import status line.

wizImportedCounts.description: First sentence of the import status line: where the table came from and its size. SOURCE is a file name (data, never translated), ROWS and COLUMNS arrive already pluralised.

wizNoHeaderRow.message: No header row found — column names were guessed (id, email, phone…); rename them in step 2.
wizNoHeaderRow.description: Second sentence of the import status line when the file had no header row. The names in the parentheses are examples of guessed column names.

wizSkippedTitleRowsOne.message: Skipped $COUNT$ title row above the header.
wizSkippedTitleRowsOne.description: Second sentence of the import status line: decorative rows above the real header were dropped.

wizSkippedTitleRowsFew.message: Skipped $COUNT$ title rows above the header.
wizSkippedTitleRowsFew.description: Second sentence of the import status line: decorative rows above the real header were dropped.

wizSkippedTitleRowsMany.message: Skipped $COUNT$ title rows above the header.
wizSkippedTitleRowsMany.description: Second sentence of the import status line: decorative rows above the real header were dropped.

wizSkippedTitleRowsOther.message: Skipped $COUNT$ title rows above the header.
wizSkippedTitleRowsOther.description: Second sentence of the import status line: decorative rows above the real header were dropped.

wizBatchRange.description: Last sentence of the import status line for a big file: which slice of the rows is being imported. The dash between the two numbers is an en dash.

wizFileRowsOne.description: Bold row count that opens the batch panel. ROWS is already grouped for the locale (40,000), so it is a formatted string, not a raw number.

wizFileRowsFew.description: Bold row count that opens the batch panel. ROWS is already grouped for the locale (40,000), so it is a formatted string, not a raw number.

wizFileRowsMany.description: Bold row count that opens the batch panel. ROWS is already grouped for the locale (40,000), so it is a formatted string, not a raw number.

wizFileRowsOther.description: Bold row count that opens the batch panel. ROWS is already grouped for the locale (40,000), so it is a formatted string, not a raw number.

wizBatchIntro.message: — a queue you walk by hand. Import a batch now; load the file again later for the next one (rows already imported merge by key).
wizBatchIntro.description: Follows the bold row count of the batch panel and finishes its sentence, so it opens with an em dash.

wizBatchRowsLabel.description: Opens the batch form row: Rows [from] to [to] · batch of [size].

wizBatchTo.description: Between the first row of the batch (an input) and the last one (a number) in the batch form row.

wizBatchSizeLabel.description: Label of the batch size input in the batch form row. Lowercase on purpose — it continues the line.

wizBatchFirstAria.description: Accessible name of the number input that picks where the batch starts.

wizBatchSizeAria.description: Accessible name of the number input that picks how many rows the batch takes.

wizBatchFirst.description: Button of the batch form row: jump back to the first N rows of the file. Lowercase on purpose.

wizBatchNext.description: Button of the batch form row: move on to the next N rows of the file. Lowercase on purpose.

wizBatchMax.description: Muted note next to the batch buttons: the hard cap on one batch.

wizContinueRolesOne.description: Primary button of wizard step 1, with the size of the batch it will carry over.

wizContinueRolesFew.description: Primary button of wizard step 1, with the size of the batch it will carry over.

wizContinueRolesMany.description: Primary button of wizard step 1, with the size of the batch it will carry over.

wizContinueRolesOther.description: Primary button of wizard step 1, with the size of the batch it will carry over.

wizNothingImported.message: Nothing imported in this session — go back to step 1 to import a list.
wizNothingImported.description: Wizard step 2 opened without a table in memory (after a reload).

wizImportSummaryOne.message: Import: $COUNT$ row · adds $ADDS$ · updates $UPDATES$ · merged within file $MERGED$ · exact duplicates $DUPES$ · excluded $EXCLUDED$
wizImportSummaryOne.description: One line of counters the user reads left to right before applying the import. Keep the counters in one line and each label next to its number.

wizImportSummaryFew.message: Import: $COUNT$ rows · adds $ADDS$ · updates $UPDATES$ · merged within file $MERGED$ · exact duplicates $DUPES$ · excluded $EXCLUDED$
wizImportSummaryFew.description: One line of counters the user reads left to right before applying the import. Keep the counters in one line and each label next to its number.

wizImportSummaryMany.message: Import: $COUNT$ rows · adds $ADDS$ · updates $UPDATES$ · merged within file $MERGED$ · exact duplicates $DUPES$ · excluded $EXCLUDED$
wizImportSummaryMany.description: One line of counters the user reads left to right before applying the import. Keep the counters in one line and each label next to its number.

wizImportSummaryOther.message: Import: $COUNT$ rows · adds $ADDS$ · updates $UPDATES$ · merged within file $MERGED$ · exact duplicates $DUPES$ · excluded $EXCLUDED$
wizImportSummaryOther.description: One line of counters the user reads left to right before applying the import. Keep the counters in one line and each label next to its number.

wizNoTargetColumn.message: Pick a target column (URL / email / @handle) — rows without a target cannot be imported.
wizNoTargetColumn.description: Blocker on wizard step 2: no column carries the role "target" yet.

wizApplyImport.description: Primary button of wizard step 2: how many rows will be written (added plus updated).

wizNamingPastePlaceholder.message: paste the answer line: id; email; phone; …
wizNamingPastePlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the input that takes the AI chat's answer. The example names show the expected shape — semicolons separate them.

wizNamingPasteAria.message: Column names from the AI answer
wizNamingPasteAria.description: Accessible name of the input that takes the AI chat's answer.

wizNamingExpectedOne.description: The pasted answer did not carry one name per column. Keep the semicolon in the quotes — it is the separator the user must type.

wizNamingExpectedFew.description: The pasted answer did not carry one name per column. Keep the semicolon in the quotes — it is the separator the user must type.

wizNamingExpectedMany.description: The pasted answer did not carry one name per column. Keep the semicolon in the quotes — it is the separator the user must type.

wizNamingExpectedOther.description: The pasted answer did not carry one name per column. Keep the semicolon in the quotes — it is the separator the user must type.

wizPromptCopied.message: Prompt copied — paste it into your AI chat, then paste the answer here.
wizPromptCopied.description: The "name these columns" prompt reached the clipboard.

wizClipboardBlocked.message: Clipboard blocked — select the names by hand.
wizClipboardBlocked.description: The browser refused clipboard access, so the prompt could not be copied.

wizCopyNamingPrompt.description: Button that copies a prompt for an AI chat. The prompt itself is sent to a model and stays English.

wizApplyNames.description: Button that renames the columns from the pasted answer line.

wizColumnNameAria.description: Accessible name of the header input in the roles table.

wizVariableTitle.description: Tooltip of the header input: the template variable this column feeds. The percent signs are spintax syntax — keep them around the name, and leave the name itself as it is.

wizRoleFor.description: Accessible name of the role dropdown. COLUMN is the user's own column header — data, never translated.

wizRoleNone.description: Role dropdown item: an ordinary column, used only as a template variable. Opens with an em dash.

wizRoleNoneHint.description: Hint under the "no role" dropdown item.

wizRoleTarget.description: Role dropdown item: the column that says where to reach the recipient. Lowercase on purpose.

wizRoleLang.description: Role dropdown item: the column that says which language the row is written in. Lowercase on purpose.

wizRoleLangHint.message: locale of the row (template per language)

wizRoleKey.description: Role dropdown item: the column that carries the user's own row key. Lowercase on purpose.

wizRoleKeyHint.message: your own row key instead of the derived one

wizSampleValue.description: Tooltip of a variable chip: the first non-empty value in that column. The value is the user's data.

wizNoValues.description: Tooltip of a variable chip whose column is empty in every row.

wizEmptyPct.description: Badge on a variable chip: the share of rows where this column is blank. Keep the percent sign next to the number.

wizConflictsOne.description: Heading of the conflicts block on wizard step 2.

wizConflictsFew.description: Heading of the conflicts block on wizard step 2.

wizConflictsMany.description: Heading of the conflicts block on wizard step 2.

wizConflictsOther.description: Heading of the conflicts block on wizard step 2.

wizConflictTwiceInFile.description: Follows the row key of a conflict: the same key appears twice in the imported file. Lowercase — it continues the line after a middle dot.

wizConflictAlreadyInCampaign.description: Follows the row key of a conflict: the key is already stored in the campaign. Lowercase — it continues the line after a middle dot.

wizConflictColField.description: Conflict table header: which field of the row differs. Lowercase on purpose.

wizConflictColCampaign.description: Conflict table header: the value stored in the campaign. Lowercase on purpose.

wizConflictColFile.description: Conflict table header: the value the imported file carries. Lowercase on purpose.

wizConflictColAction.description: Conflict table header: what to do with this field. Lowercase on purpose.

wizChoiceFillEmpty.description: Conflict choice: write the incoming value only where the stored one is blank. Lowercase on purpose.

wizChoiceKeep.description: Conflict choice: keep the value already stored in the campaign. Lowercase on purpose.

wizChoiceTake.description: Conflict choice: overwrite with the value from the imported file. Lowercase on purpose.

wizWhoWrites.description: Heading of the sender profile card on wizard step 3.

wizNoProfile.message: No sender profile yet — the form fields name / e-mail / site and %my_*% stay empty.
wizNoProfile.description: The campaign has no sender profile. %my_*% is spintax syntax for the profile variables — keep it as it is.

wizAddProfile.description: Button that opens the sender profile drawer when there is no profile yet.

wizAddAnotherProfile.description: Button that opens the sender profile drawer when the campaign already has one.

wizManageProfiles.description: Link from wizard step 3 to the profiles screen.

wizContinueProblems.description: Primary button of wizard step 3 when the template is already saved.

wizEditFullEditor.description: Link from wizard step 3 to the template screen.

wizTemplatePlaceholder.message: {Hi|Hello} %$VAR1$%, {quick|short} question about %$VAR2$% …  (paste from your AI chat or write it here)
wizTemplatePlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the small template editor on wizard step 3. The braces are spintax alternatives and the percent signs mark variables — keep both; translate the words inside the braces and the sentence in the parentheses. VAR1 and VAR2 are the campaign's own column variables.

wizSaveTemplate.description: Primary button that stores the step 1 message written on wizard step 3.

wizErrorsOne.description: Status line under the small template editor: how many errors the engine found, then the first ones.

wizErrorsFew.description: Status line under the small template editor: how many errors the engine found, then the first ones.

wizErrorsMany.description: Status line under the small template editor: how many errors the engine found, then the first ones.

wizErrorsOther.description: Status line under the small template editor: how many errors the engine found, then the first ones.

wizUnknownVars.message: Unknown variables: $VARS$ — they will render empty.
wizUnknownVars.description: The template uses variables the campaign does not have. VARS is a list of %name% tokens — spintax syntax, left as it is.

wizTemplateValid.description: The template parses. VARS is a list of %name% tokens — spintax syntax, left as it is.

wizVarsNone.description: Stands in for the variable list when the template uses no variables at all. Lowercase — it sits inside the sentence above.

wizSpintaxVars.message: Spintax with your variables: $VARS$. Includes, the AI prompt and a per-row preview live in the full editor.
wizSpintaxVars.description: Hint above the small template editor. VARS is a list of %name% tokens — spintax syntax, left as it is.

wizFullEditorLink.description: Link from the small template editor to the template screen.

wizWhatIsWritten.description: Heading of the template card on wizard step 3. "Step 1" here is the first message of the sequence, not a wizard step.

wizChipBlocking.description: Chip on wizard step 4: rows that cannot be sent as they are.

wizChipWarnings.description: Chip on wizard step 4: rows that render but look suspicious.

wizChipClean.description: Chip on wizard step 4: rows with nothing to fix.

wizChipUnchecked.message: $COUNT$ not checked here — Review checks all
wizChipUnchecked.description: Chip on wizard step 4: the screen checks the first few thousand rows only. "Review" is the name of another screen — keep it the same as the navigation item.

wizNoTemplate.message: No template yet — go back to step 3.
wizNoTemplate.description: Wizard step 4 has nothing to check because the campaign has no message yet.

wizBlockingExplain.message: Blocking: empty required variable, leaked brace, a field limit exceeded. Fix the template or the row in Review; clean rows can be approved in one click there.
wizBlockingExplain.description: Explains what counts as blocking on wizard step 4. "Review" is the name of another screen — keep it the same as the navigation item.

wizReviewCountOne.description: Link from wizard step 4 to the Review screen, with the number of rows that need attention.

wizReviewCountFew.description: Link from wizard step 4 to the Review screen, with the number of rows that need attention.

wizReviewCountMany.description: Link from wizard step 4 to the Review screen, with the number of rows that need attention.

wizReviewCountOther.description: Link from wizard step 4 to the Review screen, with the number of rows that need attention.

wizReviewAll.description: Link from wizard step 4 to the Review screen when nothing needs attention.

wizContinueQueue.description: Button of wizard step 4 that moves on to the last step.

wizHowto1.message: Open the side panel (toolbar button or the button below) — it shows the current row and its message.
wizHowto1.description: First line of the how-to list on wizard step 5.

wizHowtoOpenTarget.description: Quotes the side panel's "Open target" button inside the how-to list — must read exactly like that button.

wizHowtoOpens.description: Follows the quoted "Open target" button in the how-to list. Keep the arrow at the front.

wizHowtoFillOnSite.description: Quotes the side panel's "Fill on <host>" button inside the how-to list; site.com is a stand-in host name — must read exactly like that button.

wizHowtoFilled.message: → fields are filled, you check them and press Send on the page.
wizHowtoFilled.description: Follows the quoted "Fill on site.com" button in the how-to list. Keep the arrow at the front; "Send" is the contact form's own button on the target site.

wizHowtoSentNext.description: Quotes the side panel's "Sent — next" button inside the how-to list — must read exactly like that button.

wizHowtoRecords.message: (or S) records the outcome and moves on; other outcomes live under "Not sent…" and "More…".
wizHowtoRecords.description: Follows the quoted "Sent — next" button in the how-to list. S is the keyboard shortcut — keep the letter; the two quoted names are side panel buttons.

wizHowtoShortcuts.message: Assign your own keyboard shortcuts in the browser's extension shortcuts page if you like.
wizHowtoShortcuts.description: Last line of the how-to list on wizard step 5.

wizSeeList.description: Link from wizard step 5 to the List screen.
